changed.title: Exact obstruction lengths for extending partial group labels across one batch of vertex queries
changed.statement:
∀ (n : ℕ) (G : Type) [Group G] [DecidableEq G]
  (E : Fin n → Fin n → G → Prop),
  (∀ u v g, E u v g → E v u g⁻¹) →
  let walk := fun (m : ℕ) (v : ℕ → Fin n) (s : ℕ → G) =>
    ∀ i < m, E (v i) (v (i+1)) (s i)
  let gain := fun (m : ℕ) (s : ℕ → G) => ((List.range m).map s).prod
  let pinsOK := fun (S : Finset (Fin n)) (z : Fin n → G) (R : ℕ) =>
    ∀ m ≤ R, ∀ v s, walk m v s → v 0 ∈ S → v m ∈ S →
      z (v m) = z (v 0) * gain m s
  let closedOK := fun radius : ℕ =>
    ∀ m ≤ radius, ∀ v s, walk m v s → v 0 = v m → gain m s = 1
  ∀ (S : Finset (Fin n)) (z : Fin n → G) (q R : ℕ),
    (∀ U : Finset (Fin n), U.card ≤ q → ∃ y : Fin n → G,
      (∀ i ∈ S, y i = z i) ∧ pinsOK (S ∪ U) y R) ↔
    pinsOK S z ((q+1)*R) ∧ closedOK (q*R)
changed.unlocks: characterizes when any batch of additional vertex labels can preserve all bounded walk products
changed.context: Split a bad pinned walk into at most q+1 pieces and a bad closed walk into at most q pieces. Conversely use short walks between old and queried vertices as edges labelled by their ordered products. Contract the prescribed vertices to a root after adjusting by their values. A shortest nonidentity closed walk has no proper repeated vertex. Through the root it yields a bad old pinned walk in at most q+1 pieces, elsewhere a bad closed walk in at most q. Otherwise forest transport assigns all queried labels.

changed.title: Find a bounded nonlinear-depth selector exceeding the two-binomial-sum rank budget
changed.statement:
let nonlinear := fun (g : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Gate) =>
  (g.inputs.length == 2) &&
  xor (xor (g.op.eval [false, false]) (g.op.eval [false, true]))
      (xor (g.op.eval [true, false]) (g.op.eval [true, true]))
let depth := fun (w : ℕ) (C : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit) =>
  (C.gates.foldl (fun (ds : List ℕ) g =>
    ds ++ [(g.inputs.map (fun a => ds.getD a 0)).foldr max 0 + (nonlinear g).toNat])
    (List.replicate w 0)).getD C.output 0
∃ (n m : ℕ) (G : Fin n → Fin m → Bool) (u : Fin n) (v : Fin m),
  let entry := fun (a : Fin n) (b : Fin m) => if G a b then (1 : ZMod 2) else 0
  let A : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin m) (ZMod 2) := fun i j =>
    entry i j + entry i v + entry u j + entry u v
  let represents := fun (C : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit) =>
    (∀ g ∈ C.gates, g.inputs.length ≤ 2) ∧
    PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.NestedCover.ReadsBack (n + m) C ∧
    PEqualNP.Represents.Represents G C
  let budget := fun (t b : ℕ) =>
    (∑ j ∈ Finset.range b, Nat.choose (2*t) (j+1)) +
    (∑ j ∈ Finset.range (b-1), Nat.choose (2*t) (j+1))
  ∃ (d : ℕ) (C : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit),
    represents C ∧ depth (n+m) C ≤ d+1 ∧
    budget (C.gates.countP nonlinear) (2^d) < A.rank
changed.unlocks: tests the proposed rank budget at arbitrary nonlinear depth
changed.context: Try depth two with two nested nonlinear gates, allowing four unrelated raw affine taps. The budget is fourteen. On at least sixteen labels per bank seek at least fifteen independent rows after anchoring. Share free affine taps across banks, evaluate the table and row-reduce modulo two. Return the circuit and pivot positions. We hold no witness meeting this target.

changed.title: Connected components and at most four parity checks give the exact largest affine key flat for selected outputs on either one-round side
changed.statement:
∀ (k : ℕ) (hk : 0 < k) (column : Bool) (mark : Fin k → Bool),
  letI : ∀ p : Prop, Decidable p := Classical.propDecidable
  let K := ZMod 2
  let W := Fin k → K
  let ix := fun pos : ℕ => (⟨pos % k, Nat.mod_lt _ hk⟩ : Fin k)
  let d := if column then 2 else 1
  let g := Nat.gcd k d
  let sing := 3 ∣ k/g
  let defect := if sing then 2*g else 0
  let next := fun vertex : Fin k => ix (vertex.val+1)
  let edge := fun i j : Fin k => (mark i = true ∧ next i = j) ∨ (mark j = true ∧ next j = i)
  let price := fun S : Finset (Fin k) =>
    let step := fun left right : Fin k => left ∈ S ∧ right ∈ S ∧ edge left right
    let reach := Relation.ReflTransGen step
    let roots := S.filter (fun candidate => ∀ j ∈ S, reach candidate j → candidate.val ≤ j.val)
    let checks : Matrix (Fin g × Fin 2) roots K := fun rc root =>
      if sing then ∑ v : Fin k,
        (if v ∈ S ∧ reach root.val v ∧ v.val % g = rc.1.val ∧
            (v.val/g%3 = rc.2.val ∨ v.val/g%3 = 2) then 1 else 0) else 0
    defect + roots.card - checks.rank
  let best := (Finset.univ : Finset (Finset (Fin k))).sup price
  let independent := (Finset.univ : Finset (Finset (Fin k))).filter
    (fun A => ∀ i ∈ A, ∀ j ∈ A, i ≠ j → ¬ edge i j)
  let rot := fun (s : ℕ) (raw : W) (j : Fin k) => raw (ix (j.val+k-s%k))
  let run := fun (key name c : W) =>
    let z := rot (if column then 3 else 1) key + name
    let y := fun atMix : Fin k => z atMix + z (ix (atMix.val+d)) + z (ix (atMix.val+k-d%k))
    fun output : Fin k => y output + (1+y (ix (output.val+1))) * y (ix (output.val+2)) +
      rot (if column then 4 else 0) key output + c output
  let affineOn := fun (U : Submodule K W) (base name c : W) =>
    ∀ p : Fin k, mark p = true → ∃ (ell : W →ₗ[K] K) (b : K),
      ∀ x ∈ U, run (base+x) name c (ix (p.val+k-1)) = ell x + b
  (∀ (U : Submodule K W) (base name c : W), affineOn U base name c → Module.finrank K U ≤ best) ∧
  (∃ U : Submodule K W, Module.finrank K U = best ∧ ∀ base name c, affineOn U base name c) ∧
  (¬ sing → best = independent.sup Finset.card)
changed.unlocks: Determines the largest affine pieces for selected output sites, including both singular three-tap mixes.
changed.context: On a direction space two adjacent mixed-coordinate forms multiply affinely exactly when one is zero or they coincide. The nonzero sites therefore carry one label per connected component. The mix image requires equality of three residue parities on each singular rotation orbit. Restrict these checks to the component indicators, then add the kernel dimension when taking the preimage. Conversely all admissible component values give a flat on every translate. In the invertible case take one vertex per component or any independent set.

changed.title: It is false that: One-a-side promise: the 4 by 5 bipartite graph with mask 34940 has a fan-in-two AND/OR circuit of at most 8 gates
changed.unlocks: Proving it shows that a listed statement is false.
changed.context: The literal negation of another statement of the fleet; a counterexample to that statement proves it.
changed.sketch: Delete columns 3 and 4, each a live copy of column 2. A first reader loses a gate when its input is set to zero. Transpose the remaining table and pad a zero row, giving four-by-four mask 362. Each column contains a zero, so monotonicity forces zero when the row bank is empty. A size-eight witness would leave at most six gates, contrary to checked L-meta-5532.

changed.title: It is false that: One-a-side promise: the 4 by 6 bipartite graph with mask 268222 has a fan-in-two AND/OR circuit of at most 9 gates
changed.unlocks: Proving it shows that a listed statement is false.
changed.context: The literal negation of another statement of the fleet; a counterexample to that statement proves it.
changed.sketch: Keep columns 0,1,5 and rows 0,1,2. Delete columns 2,3,4 and row 3 one at a time. Each live duplicate costs at least one first-reader gate by fixing its wire to zero. Reorder the three rows as 0,2,1 and the three columns as 1,0,5, then pad both banks with a zero site. The result is four-by-four mask 293. A size-nine witness gives size five, contradicting checked L-meta-5506.

changed.title: A fan-in-two AND/OR/NOT circuit outputs resolution refutations of cyclic tables using the number of reachable boundary pairs
changed.statement:
∀ (n w K : ℕ) (hn : 0 < n), w ≤ n → 2 ^ w ≤ K → K ≤ 4 ^ w →
  let I := n * 2 ^ (w + 1)
  let S := (3 * (n - w) + 2) * K
  ∃ (C : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit) (enable : Fin S → ℕ)
    (memberWire : Fin S → PEqualNP.ProofComplexity.Literal (Fin n) → ℕ),
    PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.FanInTwo C ∧
    PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.NestedCover.ReadsBack I C ∧
    C.size ≤ 262144 * (n + 1) ^ 4 * K ∧ C.output < I + C.size ∧
    (∀ slot, enable slot < I + C.size) ∧
    (∀ slot lit, memberWire slot lit < I + C.size) ∧
    ∀ table : Fin n → (Fin (w + 1) → Bool) → Bool,
      let pos := fun (v : ℕ) => (⟨v % n, Nat.mod_lt _ hn⟩ : Fin n)
      let reached := fun (h : ℕ) =>
        ((Finset.univ : Finset (Fin n → Bool)).filter (fun word =>
          ∀ t : Fin h, table (pos t.val)
            (fun j => word (pos (t.val + j.val))) = true)).image
          (fun x => ((fun a : Fin w => x (pos a.val)),
                     (fun z : Fin w => x (pos (h + z.val)))))
      (∀ h ≤ n - w, (reached h).card ≤ K) →
      let inputs := List.ofFn (fun a : Fin I =>
        table (pos (a.val / 2 ^ (w + 1))) (fun bit => a.val.testBit bit.val))
      let F : Set (PEqualNP.ProofComplexity.Clause (Fin n)) :=
        {D | ∃ (i : Fin n) (p : Fin (w + 1) → Bool), table i p = false ∧
          D = Finset.univ.image (fun k : Fin (w + 1) => (pos (i.val + k.val), !(p k)))}
      let wireVal := fun wire : ℕ => (C.wires inputs).getD wire false
      let lines := ((List.finRange S).filter (fun s => wireVal (enable s))).map
        (fun s => Finset.univ.filter (fun lit => wireVal (memberWire s lit) = true))
      (C.eval inputs = true ↔ ¬ PEqualNP.ProofComplexity.Satisfiable F) ∧
        (C.eval inputs = true → PEqualNP.ProofComplexity.IsRefutation F lines ∧
          ∀ D ∈ lines, D.card ≤ 2 * w + 1)
changed.unlocks: bounds the gate cost and resolution slots needed to refute a cyclic table under the distinct-pair promise
changed.context: Start with equal windows. Batch-read both extensions of K pairs. Sort valid children by pair, mark one per group, and pack the marks with a second sort. Save both sets of switches. Test wrapping rows on final pairs. Going backward, undo packing, copy each representative clause to its duplicates, then undo the initial sort. Forbidden branches supply axioms. Forward a clause omitting the pivot or resolve. Join seed clauses likewise. Emit resolvents before premises. Charge three slots per pair and row, one per terminal pair and fewer than 2^w seed joins.

changed.title: Exact simultaneous tree-like resolution size, depth and width for inconsistent signed graph parity constraints
changed.statement:
∀ (n : ℕ) (E : Fin n → Fin n → Bool → Prop),
  (∀ u v b, E u v b → E v u b) →
  let bad := fun m : ℕ => ∃ (v : ℕ → Fin n) (s : ℕ → Bool),
    v 0 = v m ∧ Odd (((Finset.range m).filter (fun i => s i = true)).card) ∧
    ∀ i < m, E (v i) (v (i+1)) (s i)
  let ax := fun C : PEqualNP.ProofComplexity.Clause (Fin n) =>
    ∃ (u v : Fin n) (b a : Bool), E u v b ∧ C = {(u,!a),(v,a ^^ b)}
  ∀ g : ℕ, bad g → (∀ j < g, ¬ bad j) →
    ∀ L h w : ℕ,
      (∃ (nodes inner : Finset (List Bool)) (line : List Bool → PEqualNP.ProofComplexity.Clause (Fin n)),
        [] ∈ nodes ∧ inner ⊆ nodes ∧ line [] = ∅ ∧
        (∀ p ∈ nodes, p.length ≤ h ∧ (line p).card ≤ w) ∧
        (nodes \ inner).card ≤ L ∧ (∀ p ∈ nodes, p ∉ inner → ax (line p)) ∧
        (∀ (p : List Bool) (bit : Bool), p ++ [bit] ∈ nodes → p ∈ inner) ∧
        ∀ p ∈ inner, p ++ [false] ∈ nodes ∧ p ++ [true] ∈ nodes ∧
          PEqualNP.ProofComplexity.IsResolvent (line (p ++ [false])) (line (p ++ [true])) (line p)) ↔
      2*g ≤ L ∧ 2*g ≤ 2^h ∧ (if g = 1 then 1 else 2) ≤ w
changed.unlocks: determines the exact simultaneous number of axiom leaves, height and width of a signed-graph resolution tree
changed.context: The last resolution joins opposite units. Each unit subtree must contain axioms from an inconsistent signed subgraph, since on a consistent subgraph a satisfying labelling and its complement realize both values. An inconsistent subgraph contains an odd-sign cycle on distinct edges, hence each subtree has at least g leaves. Conversely split a shortest bad cycle into balanced chains. For either initial bit, compose implications along its edges in a balanced tree to derive the opposite unit. Resolve the two units. A bad loop already gives the two unit axioms.

changed.title: The 16 by 16 crown (u joined to v when u and v differ): some AND/OR circuit of fan-in at most two with at most 54 gates represents it
changed.statement: PEqualNP.Represents.RepSizeAtMost (fun u v : Fin 16 => decide (u ≠ v)) 54
changed.unlocks: the crown ladder: whether one crown beats our held circuit at n = 16
changed.context: A calibration of our constructions; no claim attached either way. Answer with a circuit: a gate list (AND or OR, at most two wires read; wires 0 to 15 left, 16 to 31 right, gate j writes wire 32+j, each gate reads only earlier wires) and the output wire, judged on all 256 inputs with one vertex on each side. We hold 55 gates: one OR per index, the indices on a 4 by 4 grid, row and column ORs, two-of on each by prefix chains, one final OR (computed). The 5 by 5 crown is exactly 15 and the 6 by 6 needs at least 18, both checked. We do not know whether 54 exists.
